unitTests.coverage: The box of the blur (radius and scale to the odd box, a box of one pixel, epsilon, a negative, NaN and an absurd radius), the rounding of premultiplying and straightening, the fixed point of a uniform picture, the running sums against a naive window sum over 7 sizes and 5 boxes (including a box wider than the picture), the spread of one pixel over two boxes, the corner insets and the rounded rectangle's clamp, the clip of a border box and a content frame, cap insets as margins in pixels, and paint(): which of tint, caps, tiling and clip a draw keeps for a plain (blurred) picture, a stretch, a repeat and a cover

checkIdDigest: SHA-256 of the check ids joined by newlines, in the order the probe ran them

lanes.meaning: Current host, headless: 52 declared Images (blur, tint, caps, mask and ignored props), 13 live changes, the network stage over the loopback Node server (6 steps over the two caches), the RID lifecycle and the stop, then the independent oracle over the report.

The same bundle on the host built from main fb50a32 (no effects); expected negative control (--allow-original-negative). The probe runs every stage: the 13 checks that hold on every host pass and the 40 normative ones fail.

combined/A tinted nine-patch in a rounded view is one item: the tint, the mask and the nine-patch are declared together
network/A blurred request downloads, decodes, blurs and keeps its picture to itself: the decoded cache holds nothing, and the byte cache holds the response
network/The plain request after it is answered from the byte cache and decodes the pixels of the file: no blurred pixel went into the decoded cache
network/A blurred request does not read the decoded cache, though it holds the picture: it takes the bytes and blurs them, and the cache is as it was
network/Each view draws what it was given, tinted, masked or blurred, over the same picture; the live textures are the cached one and the two blurred, no more
network/Blurring an Image that showed the cached picture asks again, with no onLoadStart, and reads nothing from the decoded cache
network/Clearing the blur finds the cached picture again, without the network
lifecycle/Every Image that has a picture has one item of its own, and every Image that tints or clips has one material: the RIDs made and freed are the live ones
lifecycle/One shader serves every view, made the first time one needed it, and it is freed with the extension, not with a view
lifecycle/Unmounting a tinted Image frees its item and its material, and unmounting a plain one frees its item alone
lifecycle/Mounting it again makes an item and a material of its own and does not make the shader again
lifecycle/Unmounting a root frees the items and materials of its Images, and only theirs
lifecycle/When the application stops and its views are gone, no item and no material is left, no texture outlives it, and the shader still waits for the extension to end

oracle.independence: Written apart from the probe and from the C++. It recomputes the blurred bitmap of every blurred Image pixel by pixel (premultiply with rounding, two square box passes with the edge extended and one rounding of the exact window mean, straighten) and compares its fingerprint with the worker's; it derives the layout, the radii (percentages, the CSS overlap rule, the corner insets and the rounded rectangle's clamp), the tint, the cap-inset margins, the draw rectangles and the parameters of the material for each declared case from the declared style and props and compares them to what the view asked the renderer for within a thousandth; it replays the 13 live changes over the declared state; and it models what each of the six network steps must do to the two caches, reading the server's own log. It reuses the independent content-mode helper of tests/images-oracle.mjs

implementation.subject: fix(images): Guard the blur buffer size and share the asset sampler

executedTree.note: The tree of the review commit, which holds the merges of main after 6c221e8; every lane below ran on it, with no uncommitted change (git status was empty before the runs)

causes.finding: width * height and count * 4 were computed without a size_t overflow check, so dimensions no bitmap has made a count that wraps (to zero, or to a small buffer size) and the function could read and write past the buffer it was given
logoAt repeated the supersampling loop that drawn runs for every other asset, so two loops had to be kept equal; logoAt now delegates to drawn

changes.blurGuard: box_blur_rgba8 returns without touching the buffer when width > SIZE_MAX / height or when width * height > SIZE_MAX / 4, after the early return for a zero side or a kernel of one pixel; every real size (and the 7 sizes x 5 boxes the test compares with the naive blur) is blurred as before
changes.unitTest: native/image_effects_test.cpp gains the group dimensions_that_overflow_leave_the_buffer, called after the group of the uniform picture: 2^63 x 2 (a pixel count that wraps to zero), SIZE_MAX x 3 (a count that overflows) and SIZE_MAX / 4 + 1 x 1 (a pixel count that fits and a byte count that does not) must leave the buffer as it was. The test has 11 groups and 49 assertions (it had 10 and 46)
changes.assetSampler: drawn moved above logoAt, and logoAt(size) is drawn(size, shade) with the logo's shade (null outside the rounded square); the one loop serves the logo, the icon, the avatar and the panel

lanes.meaning: The content frame is clipped with the view's radii whole, as if the border had no width (native/image_effects_core.h).
failedIds: mask/A view that clips and has radii clips its picture to the border box with the radii, and to the content frame with each radius less the border beside it, limited as RCTPathCreateWithRoundedRect limits them
mask/The shader's coordinates are the pixels of the picture: at scale 3 every point is three

lanes.meaning: The blur makes a third box pass; RN iOS's picture is the result of the second of its three convolutions (native/image_effects_core.h).
failedIds: blur/Every blurred bitmap is, byte for byte, the one the manifest holds for its picture and its box: two passes, in premultiplied alpha, the edge extended
network/A blurred request downloads, decodes, blurs and keeps its picture to itself: the decoded cache holds nothing, and the byte cache holds the response
network/Blurring an Image that showed the cached picture asks again, with no onLoadStart, and reads nothing from the decoded cache

lanes.meaning: A blurred request reads and writes the decoded cache like a plain one (native/image_loader.cpp).
failedIds: network/A blurred request downloads, decodes, blurs and keeps its picture to itself: the decoded cache holds nothing, and the byte cache holds the response
network/The plain request after it is answered from the byte cache and decodes the pixels of the file: no blurred pixel went into the decoded cache
network/A blurred request does not read the decoded cache, though it holds the picture: it takes the bytes and blurs them, and the cache is as it was
network/A tinted view and a masked view of the cached picture are answered by the decoded cache: they share its picture, and no texture is made
network/Each view draws what it was given, tinted, masked or blurred, over the same picture; the live textures are the cached one and the two blurred, no more
network/Blurring an Image that showed the cached picture asks again, with no onLoadStart, and reads nothing from the decoded cache
network/and the cached picture, shown by two other views, is as it was
network/Clearing the blur finds the cached picture again, without the network

lanes.meaning: capInsets are taken as pixels of the picture, not points: the margins ignore the scale (native/image_effects_core.h).
failedIds: caps/capInsets as a number or an object of top, left, bottom and right become a nine-patch of the whole picture over the content frame, with margins in the pixels of the picture and the modes of the resize mode
caps/Setting, changing and clearing capInsets redraws at once with no request: a nine-patch, another and the plain picture

notDepartures: A picture that RCTBlurredImageWithRadius rebuilds from its bitmap has none of the template mode, the caps and the tiling of the image it was given, so a blurred Image takes no tint and no capInsets and repeat fills the view with it (RCTImageComponentView.mm:144-168, RCTImageBlurUtils.mm:85-96); a box of one pixel returns the input image untouched, so that one keeps all three

The props that the iOS view config drops never reach the native side and defaultSource is parsed and read by no component (ImageViewNativeComponent.js:133-153, ReactNativeAttributePayload.js:73-74 and 246-247, ImageProps.cpp:22-27 and 82-87); accepting them without effect is what iOS does

A view that clips clips its picture to the border box with the radii and to the content frame with each radius less the border beside it (RCTViewComponentView.mm:1300-1337 with enableIOSViewClipToPaddingBox false, RCTBorderDrawing.m:43-61 and 104-130); ViewProps has already applied the CSS overlap rule to the radii it resolves (BaseViewProps.cpp:415-468 and 506-524), so a radius of 999 on a 40-point view is 20
departuresFromRN: The blur is not bit-identical to vImage's: vImageBoxConvolve_ARGB8888 is closed, so the host states its own arithmetic. Premultiply round(c a / 255), two square box passes whose window mean is rounded to the nearest once (an odd divisor leaves no tie), straighten round(p 255 / a) capped at 255, black where a is 0; a box wider than 2^20 pixels is limited to it

tintColor, capInsets and borderRadius take effect on the next draw. On iOS the template mode and the caps are applied when an image response arrives (RCTImageComponentView.mm:144-155), so a change of tintColor waits for the next response, and clearing it leaves a template image tinted by the window

onLoad comes after the blur: the worker blurs before the texture exists and the view is told then. On iOS onLoad and onLoadEnd are sent before the blur is made (RCTImageComponentView.mm:139-140, 157-168), with the same payload

capInsets as a list [left, top, right, bottom] is refused. graphicsConversions.h:147-180 reads a list, but it tries the object form first (155) and a list passes for an object with the keys 0 to 3, so RN logs 'Unsupported EdgeInsets map key' for each and keeps no inset; the wrapper says so instead of dropping it

capInsets apply to the stretch and repeat modes only; cover, contain, center and none draw as they do without them. What UIKit does with a resizable image under those content modes was not verified, nor how it tiles the edges of a tiled nine-patch, nor what it does when the view is smaller than the caps (Godot does not limit the margins to the destination; the host limits them to the picture)

A fully transparent black tintColor (0x00000000, what 'transparent' is) is not a tint: RN's C++ color for this host is one integer in which zero is 'no color' (Color.h:56-59, HostPlatformColor.h:19), where iOS has a defined clear UIColor and the template image disappears. Any other fully transparent color is a tint

The border of a view is painted below the picture here (the view's own item draws it, the picture's item comes after) and above it on iOS (the border layer's zPosition); with the clip rules above the picture never reaches the border, so nothing differs in what is seen

The picture's clip, tint and caps are one shader on an item of its own, scaled by 1/scale; a blurred picture has a texture of its own that no cache holds, and every other picture's texture is the cache's and is never written
limits: The renderer of a headless run is Godot's dummy, which draws no pixel and ignores the parameters of a material: the probe and the oracle certify what the view asked the renderer for (rectangles, radii, margins, tint, the item and the material it made) and the exact pixels of the blur by the bitmap the worker made; only the example's capture lane saw the shader draw

The capture lane samples a few points of the saved frame (the icon's dot, ring, body and corner, the soft and the sharp landscape at the sun's edge and in the sky, the card's border at two places of both cards, the avatars' corner, edge and centre, and the second avatar's border and round corner); there is no independent pixel oracle of the whole frame

No comparison with UIKit was made: the blur's box and rounding, the tiling of a nine-patch, the resizable image under the other content modes and the template rendering were not compared on an iOS device

A blur at the content scale of a picture whose box is wider than the picture (radius 30 at scale 3 on a 36x27 pixel picture) was checked against the oracle's own blur; the blur of very large pictures and its time were not measured on a device

Animated GIF and WebP, nativeImageSource, defaultSource's placeholder, loadingIndicatorSource and fadeDuration's transition (which iOS does not have), resizeMethod and resizeMultiplier (Android's) are not delivered, and an Image inside Text is a failure by design
Assets and network pictures were loaded in the project's own run, against a loopback server; no exported app, desktop export or Android export ran

Hosted macOS CI has not run this slice; the oracle and the probe state values from what the host delivered or from model states, never from frame pace or from how bytes were segmented, and every wait is bounded by time and ends on a state
Only macOS arm64 was executed; Windows, Linux, Android, iOS and Web runtimes are not covered
GF-16 is open: this third slice closes no checkpoint, and no whole GF, contract, parity, target, weight or denominator closes.
